questions.q: What is the key difference between cleansing and standardization?
options: Cleansing fixes values that are factually wrong; standardization makes correct-but-inconsistent values uniform
They are two names for the exact same operation
Cleansing only applies to numbers; standardization only applies to text
Standardization deletes bad rows; cleansing merges duplicates
questions.explain: "NY" and "New York" are both correct but inconsistent — that's a standardization problem, not a cleansing one.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four core cleansing operations named in this lesson?
options: Visualizing
Parsing
Correcting
Enriching
questions.explain: The four named operations are parsing, correcting, deduplicating, and enriching. Visualizing isn't a cleansing operation.

questions.q: What does it mean for a cleansing script to be "idempotent"?
options: Running it a second time doesn't change the result any further
It can only ever be run exactly once
It automatically generates its own audit trail
It only works on numeric columns
questions.explain: A script that only touches rows still needing the fix, like the lesson's UPDATE example, is safe to re-run without double-correcting rows.

questions.q: Why does a cleansing step need an audit trail?
options: So the original value, the rule that changed it, and when it changed are all defensible evidence later, for root cause work or an audit
It's required by SQL syntax
It makes the script run faster
It automatically standardizes new values going forward
questions.explain: Silently overwriting the original value destroys the evidence a later investigation or auditor would need.

questions.q: Why can a dataset pass every cleansing check and still fail for reporting purposes?
options: If standardization was skipped, correct-but-inconsistent values (like ten spellings of one customer name) won't group or deduplicate properly
Reporting tools always require a NoSQL database
Cleansing checks are stricter than reporting requirements
This situation can't actually happen
questions.explain: Every individual value can be 'accurate' and still break a GROUP BY or deduplication step if it isn't written consistently.
